paragraphs: The paper explores ritual as a way to design AI experiences for groups. Its setting is an immersive UCLA production of the roller disco musical Xanadu, where audience participation became part of the performance. Across a two-week run, more than five hundred audience members contributed drawings and jazzercise movements, with vision-language models mediating interactions involving virtual scenery and choreographic prompts.

The authors interpret these interactions through four aspects of ritual. Audience contributions functioned as offerings that AI transformed into parts of the shared experience. Performers acted as guides, showing people how to participate and organizing them into groups. The AI systems also functioned as instruments: their sensing, generation, and stage effects formed something humans could learn to control through practice. Finally, interaction was reciprocal, with the machinery shaping participants’ behavior while their actions visibly changed the virtual world.

This framing helped bring audience interaction together with the show’s story, characters, and music. Its significance is a concrete exploration of how AI can participate in collective creativity and play, extending attention beyond interfaces designed around one person. The production illustrates how human guidance, audience contributions, and responsive AI can become interconnected parts of a shared performance.
neurips-2025-ai-as-intermediary-in-moder.tldr: An immersive production of Xanadu explored ritual as a framework for shared human–AI creativity, connecting audience participation, performer guidance, and responsive virtual scenery.

paragraphs: This study asks whether automated creativity assessments respond to ideas themselves or to the way language models express them. It investigates a recurring pattern: model responses receive high originality scores while varying less than human responses. The authors call this combination the LLM creativity paradox.

The researchers collected responses from seven language models on a modified Alternative Uses Task and compared them with responses from thirty people. Four automated tools scored both the original model outputs and versions rewritten to reduce verbosity while preserving their central ideas. This comparison tests how changing presentation affects assessments without intentionally changing the proposed concepts.

Rewording substantially reduced originality scores and slightly increased variability. However, the rewritten model responses still scored as more original and less variable than human responses. Style therefore explains part of the measured paradox, rather than eliminating it. The findings support caution when automated scores inform creative feedback: a change in wording can alter the assessment even when the underlying idea remains.
neurips-2025-ai-is-misled-by-genai-styli.tldr: Automated creativity scores partly reward language-model writing style, although differences from human responses persist after rewording.

paragraphs: Assembloid Agency proposes an open-source connection between Unreal Engine environments and living neurons grown on high-density electrode arrays. The idea is to make a game engine an experimental interface for biological computing, allowing researchers to design simulated situations that interact with neuronal cultures.

The proposed plugin would expose functions for stimulating neurons, recording their activity, visualizing signals, and controlling interactions in real time. Researchers could prototype contexts using biological cultures, spiking neural networks, or EEG substitutes. Planned game templates would build on Unreal’s Learning Agents plugin and support reinforcement-learning scenarios involving one or multiple organoids.

The broader contribution is a design perspective: experimental environments help shape the interaction between biological and synthetic participants. Games offer ways to construct those environments and explore how agency is distributed across them. The abstract presents an API proposal and anticipated applications, including interactive experiences and AI benchmarking, while foregrounding ethical and aesthetic guardrails for work with organoid intelligence.
neurips-2025-assembloid-agency-unreal-en.tldr: Assembloid Agency proposes an Unreal Engine interface for designing interactive experiments with living neuronal cultures.

paragraphs: This paper approaches computational painting as a sequence of actions. Its central concern is how an artwork develops through organized brush movements, from establishing the composition to refining smaller details. That shifts attention toward the order and regional organization of painting decisions, which a finished image alone does not directly display.

The method uses image vectorization to identify meaningful painting regions. Algorithms then estimate brushstroke parameters and choose sequences that move from broad compositional structure toward localized refinement. The resulting representation links where a stroke belongs with when it should appear during the reconstructed painting process.

The output includes animations that build an image stroke by stroke, making the computational reconstruction visible over time. These sequences are intended to resemble a more natural artistic workflow. The paper proposes applications in immersive museum experiences and collaborative art tools, where watching or interacting with the sequence could become part of the experience. Its contribution is a method for generating an organized painting process.
neurips-2025-brushes-in-motion-vector-gu.tldr: The method reconstructs paintings as region-aware brushstroke sequences that develop from broad composition to fine detail.

paragraphs: This paper treats the design of planar mechanical linkages as a problem of generating images across related domains. The authors construct RGB representations of mechanisms ranging from simple four-bar and sliding arrangements to more complex eight-bar linkages. This gives different mechanical designs a common visual format for a generative model.

A shared-latent variational autoencoder connects the representations to explore previously unseen motion curves and novel mechanism behavior. The approach also encodes the speed of points along a trajectory through color gradients. Consequently, a desired movement can specify both the path a point should follow and how its speed should vary along that path.

The authors evaluate the method on three datasets with increasing mechanical complexity, including multi-loop mechanisms. Their preliminary results support image representations as a useful basis for generative mechanical design. The demonstrated scope includes rotating and sliding joints; extending the same framework to cams and gears remains a stated possibility. The appeal is a unified representation for connecting desired motion with mechanism design.
neurips-2025-creative-synthesis-of-kinem.tldr: An image-generative approach designs planar linkages using visual representations of mechanisms, motion paths, and speed profiles.

paragraphs: The Cultural Alien Sampler addresses a tension in generating artistic ideas: familiar combinations can be coherent but predictable, while unusual combinations can lose internal consistency. Its solution is to evaluate these qualities separately, making originality a targeted departure from learned conventions rather than simply selecting concepts at random.

The method uses two GPT-2 models fine-tuned on WikiArt concepts. One estimates whether concepts plausibly belong together in an artwork. The other estimates how typical their combination is within individual artists’ work. The sampler favors combinations with strong compositional fit and low cultural typicality, seeking ideas that make sense together while avoiding familiar pairings.

In a human evaluation involving one hundred participants, the approach exceeded random selection and GPT-4o baselines and performed comparably to human art students on perceived originality and harmony. A separate quantitative analysis found greater diversity and broader conceptual exploration than GPT-4o. These results support the usefulness of separating coherence from typicality for the artistic concept-selection setting studied.
neurips-2025-cultural-alien-sampler-open.tldr: Separately scoring conceptual fit and cultural typicality helps generate artistic ideas judged both original and harmonious.

paragraphs: EMPATHIA is a multi-agent framework for refugee integration that explicitly includes cultural, emotional, and ethical considerations. It addresses allocation decisions in which employment or another single objective cannot capture all relevant values. Its design is grounded in Kegan’s Constructive Developmental Theory and emphasizes collaboration with human practitioners.

The framework divides integration into initial placement, early independence, and sustained outcomes through the SEED, RISE, and THRIVE modules. SEED uses a selector–validator architecture with specialized emotional, cultural, and ethical agents. Their deliberation is designed to make recommendations interpretable, while weighted factors provide a way to reconcile competing considerations.

The authors report experiments using the UN Kakuma dataset and an implementation involving 6,359 working-age refugees with more than 150 socioeconomic variables. They report 87.4% validation convergence and explainable assessments across five host countries. These findings concern the framework’s recommendation and validation process. The broader proposed contribution is an approach to allocation that helps practitioners consider multiple value systems in consequential decisions.
neurips-2025-empathia-multi-faceted-huma.tldr: EMPATHIA combines specialized agents to support interpretable refugee-integration recommendations across cultural, emotional, and ethical priorities.

paragraphs: This study tests whether prompts can steer language models toward different moral perspectives. The authors create seven equally long constitutions, each containing ten principles. These include perspectives such as ecological justice and Ubuntu, alongside neutral and random-adjective conditions that help distinguish meaningful moral framing from merely adding prompt text.

Four models generate 2,800 responses to a benchmark covering everyday advice, policy scenarios, normative dilemmas, and rewriting. Evaluation considers toxicity, semantic agreement with each constitution’s reference ideas, characteristic vocabulary, and a model-based judgment combining authenticity, helpfulness, and safety. This examines several aspects of response behavior rather than relying on one alignment score.

Meaningful moral frames consistently improve measured alignment and judged quality without increasing measured toxicity; the placebo prompts do not. Effects appear across the tested models and are strongest on morally charged tasks. The accompanying open-source toolkit supports authoring additional frames. The findings establish prompting as a practical means of producing value-conditional behavior in the studied settings, with potential uses in participatory and creative AI.
neurips-2025-encoding-values-injecting-m.tldr: Ten-principle moral prompts steer tested language models toward different value frameworks while improving judged quality without increasing measured toxicity.

paragraphs: This paper uses chess to examine whether strong AI performance corresponds to representations of human strategic concepts. The authors analyze a 270-million-parameter transformer capable of grandmaster-level play, asking how concepts such as center control and knight outposts appear at different depths inside the model.

Early layers encode the studied concepts with accuracy reaching 85%, while deeper layers fall to 50–65% despite contributing to stronger play. The authors also introduce 240 expert-annotated Chess960 positions covering six strategic concepts. Randomized starting positions remove familiar opening theory, providing a test of concept recognition beyond conventional opening patterns.

Across the tested methods, concept recognition drops by 10–20% in this setting. The authors interpret this as evidence of reliance on memorized patterns and a divergence between performance-oriented representations and human strategic language. The results highlight a collaboration challenge: a model can play exceptionally well while its internal representations become less aligned with concepts people use to reason about the game.
neurips-2025-exploring-human-ai-conceptu.tldr: A strong chess transformer shows weaker alignment with human strategic concepts in deeper layers and on randomized starting positions.

paragraphs: This work presents a geometric algorithm developed through human–AI collaboration for generating origami shuriken assemblies. It combines mathematical design rules with interactive software and fabrication workflows. The central aim is to explore a large family of related artworks while retaining a connection between digital designs and physical construction.

The algorithm uses radial symmetry, affine transformations, and programmable crease patterns. Its mathematical framework describes assemblies with cyclic symmetry, expressed as Z_n symmetry, where repeated elements are organized around a center. These ingredients provide a structured way to vary an assembly while preserving the geometric organization that defines the design family.

The contributions also include a fabrication-compatible algorithm and a web application for real-time co-design. Together, they connect analytic theory, interactive exploration, and making. The project illustrates how generative AI can contribute to a collaborative design process spanning digital and physical work. Its creative significance lies in using programmable geometry to reinterpret a historical form and explore many possible configurations.
neurips-2025-human-ai-co-development-of-.tldr: A human–AI-developed geometry framework supports interactive design and fabrication of radially symmetric origami shuriken assemblies.

paragraphs: Human-Machine Ritual presents a motion-recognition system for performance in which a machine responds to a dancer’s movements. It combines wearable inertial sensors, a time-series classifier called MiniRocket, and multimedia control. The goal is a responsive creative relationship that preserves the expressive role of the performer’s body.

Movement-to-sound mappings are specific to the dancer and draw on bodily memory and association. This makes recognition part of an individual expressive practice: the system observes movement patterns and connects them to responsive sound. The technical components support this relationship by translating a stream of sensor measurements into recognized movements that can drive multimedia responses.

The authors report high classification accuracy with latency below fifty milliseconds. They present the lightweight design as a replicable framework for creative, educational, and live performance settings. The contribution brings together responsive recognition and a human-centered mapping process, showing how machine learning can support attentive interaction with a performer while keeping embodied expression central to the experience.
neurips-2025-human-machine-ritual-synerg.tldr: Wearable sensors and fast movement classification enable dancer-specific sound responses for collaborative human–machine performance.

paragraphs: This paper defines interactive artistic text-to-voice as a task for vocal synthesis in live creative settings. Although synthesized speech has become increasingly realistic, the authors identify limited support for real-time artistic applications. Their system targets low latency, interactive control, and the exploration of unconventional vocal expression.

The architecture combines a character-level text encoder, streaming alignment based on Tacotron2, and a RAVE streaming vocoder. These components connect text processing with ongoing voice generation. Streaming is central to the intended performance setting, where the system needs to respond as the artist interacts with it rather than only produce a completed recording afterward.

The authors release Tungnaá, an open-source Python package covering model training and real-time inference, together with a graphical interface for experimental music performance. They also describe training strategies for small artist-created datasets and an artistic collaboration with sound poet Jaap Blonk. The contribution combines a task definition, working software, and a performance application organized around expressive vocal interaction.
neurips-2025-interactive-artistic-text-t.tldr: Tungnaá supports low-latency, controllable text-to-voice synthesis for experimental vocal performance using artist-created training data.

paragraphs: LUMIA turns looking at the surrounding environment into an input for musical composition. Its handheld camera interface lets people frame and capture visual scenes, then use those scenes to generate musical phrases. The project is designed around tactile improvisation and environmental interaction rather than a workflow centered on detailed parameter adjustment.

GPT-4V analyzes captured images and produces structured prompts. Those prompts are combined with the user’s chosen instrumentation and passed to Stable Audio to generate music. Users can interactively capture material and layer the resulting loopable segments, connecting visual selection with the development of a musical composition.

The division of creative influence is explicit: the person chooses what to look at and which instruments to use, while the models interpret the scene and generate audio. The system demonstrates a physical interface linking vision, language, and sound. Its contribution is a mode of co-creation in which sensory attention and bodily interaction with the environment help guide the musical result.
neurips-2025-lumia-a-handheld-vision-to-.tldr: LUMIA converts camera-captured scenes and user-selected instrumentation into loopable music through a handheld, interactive workflow.

paragraphs: MambaKit combines neural generation with deterministic musical structure to synthesize individual drum sounds. It aims to give users understandable controls while allowing a learned model to handle acoustic complexity. The design addresses the difficulty of choosing between largely opaque generation and traditional synthesis that demands substantial specialist knowledge.

During training, the system automatically extracts controls including root-note-derived sine anchors, pitch envelopes, and ADSR parameters. These become interpretable controls during generation. A structured diffusion framework combines harmonic anchors with learned noise injection, while a frequency-aware MAMBA2 architecture matches temporal processing windows to signal characteristics.

The authors report up to 256-fold memory efficiency and 44.1-kHz raw-audio synthesis on a single A100 GPU. They describe production-quality output from the first training batch of two samples, with occasional instabilities diminishing after minimal additional training. Complete arrangements made exclusively from MambaKit samples demonstrate practical use. The results suggest that explicit musical structure and human controls can support capable generation without relying solely on computational scaling.
neurips-2025-mambakit-towards-modular-in.tldr: MambaKit combines interpretable musical controls with neural drum synthesis, reporting high-quality audio and substantial memory efficiency.

paragraphs: NeuralPLexer3 is a generative model for predicting the structures of biomolecular complexes. Such structures help explain how biological molecules interact, making them relevant to understanding disease mechanisms and developing therapeutics. The paper addresses the continuing challenge of making computational structure prediction useful for real-world drug discovery.

The proposed model uses a physics-inspired, flow-based approach. The authors report state-of-the-art prediction accuracy for key biomolecular interaction types, together with improved training and sampling efficiency compared with predecessors and alternative methods. Both accuracy and efficiency matter to the stated goal of moving structure prediction toward practical discovery workflows.

Evaluation uses existing and new benchmarks and emphasizes blind docking, physical validity, and protein shape changes induced by ligands. These focus areas connect predicted structures with the interaction questions that arise in structure-based drug design. The reported findings therefore concern several aspects of useful complex prediction, including where molecules bind and how binding relates to protein conformation, alongside the efficiency of producing predictions.
neurips-2025-neuralplexer3-accurate-biom.tldr: NeuralPLexer3 reports accurate, efficient biomolecular complex prediction using a physics-inspired flow model, with strengths relevant to drug design.

paragraphs: Opt-In Art asks whether learning an artistic style from a few examples requires a model to have already seen paintings during pretraining. To investigate, the authors first train a text-to-image model entirely on photographs, excluding painting-related content. They then adapt that model to an artistic style using a small set of examples.

User studies and automated evaluations find that the adapted model performs comparably to state-of-the-art models trained on large datasets containing paintings, drawings, or illustrations. This demonstrates the possibility of acquiring the evaluated artistic styles through limited adaptation even when the initial training data excludes paintings.

The authors also use data attribution to examine how artistic and non-artistic datasets contribute to generated images. Their findings suggest that high-quality artistic output can be achieved without artistic pretraining data. The proposed significance is a more controlled route to style generation: a photograph-trained foundation can acquire artistic characteristics from a limited, deliberately selected collection supplied during adaptation.
neurips-2025-opt-in-art-learning-art-sty.tldr: A model pretrained only on photographs can learn artistic styles from a few examples and match evaluated art-pretrained models after adaptation.

paragraphs: ProGress addresses structural coherence and interpretability in symbolic music generation. The authors focus particularly on relationships between harmony and melody, arguing that existing generative systems often fail to organize these relationships coherently. Their approach brings concepts from Schenkerian musical analysis into a diffusion-based generation framework.

The system adapts DiGress, a discrete diffusion model, for music generation. It also introduces a phrase-fusion method inspired by Schenkerian analysis, connecting the assembly of musical phrases with a structured analytical perspective. User controls over aspects of generation are included as part of the framework, making human influence an explicit component of composition.

Together, these elements aim to produce music whose organization is both coherent and musically interpretable. Human experiments suggest stronger performance than existing state-of-the-art methods. The stated result supports combining learned generation with music-theoretic structure in the evaluated setting. The broader contribution is a framework that connects generative modeling, phrase organization, and user control within the same compositional process.
neurips-2025-progress-structured-music-g.tldr: ProGress combines discrete diffusion, hierarchical musical analysis, and user controls to support coherent, interpretable music generation.

paragraphs: This paper proposes a recommendation workflow for small design interventions in public spaces. It combines computer vision with human selection so that suggestions can reflect the objects already present in a scene. The broader aim is to support ongoing, local participation in urban design through choices grounded in everyday spatial patterns.

The system uses Grounding DINO and a curated subset of ADE20K as a proxy for the urban built environment. Detected objects are used to build co-occurrence embeddings that capture common configurations. After a user chooses an anchor object, the system recommends five statistically likely complementary objects.

A vision-language model then considers the scene image and the selected pair to propose a third object, developing a more complex intervention. People retain control over selection and refinement throughout the process. The method combines statistical familiarity with scene-based reasoning: common combinations provide initial options, and contextual interpretation extends the chosen arrangement. Its intended contribution is participatory design support for localized public-space decisions.
neurips-2025-scene-aware-urban-design-a-.tldr: A human-guided urban design workflow combines object co-occurrence patterns and vision-language reasoning to suggest small public-space interventions.

paragraphs: Semantic Glitch is a soft flying robotic artwork shaped like a three-dimensional pixel cloud. The project explores how an intentionally imprecise robot can develop a compelling character. Its physical design draws on digital archaeology, connecting the robot’s appearance with its broader artistic treatment of imperfection.

The navigation pipeline relies on a multimodal language model’s qualitative interpretation instead of conventional LiDAR sensing or SLAM-based mapping. A natural-language prompt supplies a biologically inspired personality. This combines a semantically guided decision process with a body that lacks precise awareness of its own physical state.

The authors analyze a thirteen-minute autonomous flight log and conduct a follow-up study that statistically supports the framework’s ability to produce measurably distinct personas. They observe landmark-based navigation and a gap between intended plans and executed actions. These behaviors contribute to unpredictable but plausible characterization. The work presents an artistic robotics framework whose evaluated purpose emphasizes authored personality and expressive companionship over efficient, precise movement.
neurips-2025-semantic-glitch-agency-and-.tldr: A flying pixel-cloud artwork uses language-model navigation and prompted personalities to turn physical imprecision into expressive character.

paragraphs: Sensorium Arc presents ocean data through spoken interaction with AI agents that adopt the ocean’s perspective. The installation combines scientific material with poetic expression, making environmental data part of an immersive narrative. Its aim is to offer an intuitive and emotional route into complex marine information.

The system uses a modular multi-agent architecture and a retrieval-augmented language-model framework. As a conversation unfolds, keyword detection and semantic parsing identify references to times, locations, and themes. These cues trigger relevant data visualizations and audiovisual material, linking the spoken exchange with a changing multimedia experience.

Developed with the Center for the Study of the Force Majeure and inspired by Newton Harrison’s ecological aesthetics, the project treats the ocean as a poetic speaker. Its contribution is a demonstration of how conversational interfaces can coordinate data exploration and ecological art. The abstract presents this as a potential way to mediate access to high-dimensional environmental data through affective engagement and responsive storytelling.
neurips-2025-sensorium-arc-ai-agent-syst.tldr: Sensorium Arc combines ocean-themed conversation, retrieved information, and responsive audiovisual displays to make marine data an interactive artistic experience.

paragraphs: Stroke Patches presents an image-styling method built around explicit choices about the strokes used to render an image. The approach uses regression and a configurable collection of stroke patches. Its central contribution is control over stroke composition and the amount of visual detail in the resulting artwork.

Small programs generate the patches procedurally. They specify properties including stroke shape, size, orientation, density, color, and noise. This makes the training material itself a means of defining the visual style: the appearance of individual patches is determined through adjustable stroke properties, and the collection can be extended with additional patches.

A U-Net-based regression model is trained on a patch set and then renders input images in customizable artistic styles. The method connects procedural decisions about local marks with learned image rendering. Its significance is that customization is expressed through concrete stroke characteristics, giving users a way to shape the visual vocabulary and detail level of the output through the patch sets used for training.
neurips-2025-stroke-patches-customizable.tldr: Procedurally generated stroke patches train a regression model to stylize images with explicit control over stroke composition and detail.

paragraphs: This paper connects text-based 3D generation with robotic assembly of objects containing different component types. The central problem is deciding how a generated shape should be realized using predefined structural and panel pieces. Geometry alone does not capture every decision, because the object’s intended function also affects where panels belong.

The pipeline uses a vision-language model for zero-shot reasoning about both shape and functionality. It decomposes generated meshes into component-based models and determines which regions need panels in addition to structural elements. Users can then refine these assignments through conversational feedback, keeping a direct role in shaping the physical design.

Across test objects, the authors report user preference rates of 90.6% for the model-generated assignments, 59.4% for rule-based assignments, and 2.5% for random assignments. These results support the usefulness of functional reasoning for the component-selection task studied. The broader contribution links generated geometry, component decisions, robotic making, and conversational refinement within one workflow.
neurips-2025-text-to-robotic-assembly-of.tldr: Vision-language reasoning turns generated 3D meshes into structural-and-panel assembly plans that users can refine conversationally.

paragraphs: The Anemoia Device is an interactive artwork designed to evoke nostalgia for a time the user has never experienced. It begins with an archival photograph and transforms it into a multisensory artifact. The project uses synthetic memory as a creative premise for exploring how AI may participate in experiences of remembering.

Its pipeline brings together vision, language, and scent technologies. A physical interface with dials lets the user guide a language model’s translation from semantic meaning into an olfactory expression. The photograph therefore becomes the starting point for an interpretation that extends beyond an image into another sensory medium.

The contribution combines this cross-modal process with an intentional physical ritual. Turning the dials gives the user an active part in shaping the artifact, making co-authorship central to the interaction. The work is presented as an inquiry into the malleability of memory in an age of AI, with embodied participation providing an alternative form of engagement to a conventional screen-based interface.
neurips-2025-the-anemoia-device-a-tangib.tldr: The Anemoia Device uses archival photographs, generative AI, scent, and physical dials to co-create experiences of imagined nostalgia.

paragraphs: Aria-Duet lets a human pianist and a generative music model collaborate through the same physical piano. The project addresses the mismatch between text-prompted music generation and the embodied responsiveness of instrumental playing. A Yamaha Disklavier serves as the shared interface, allowing model-generated material to be performed acoustically.

The interaction follows a turn-taking pattern. The pianist plays a passage and signals a handover; the Aria model then generates a continuation that the piano performs. The technical architecture supports low-latency exchanges, connecting model generation with a performance workflow organized around musical contributions rather than written descriptions.

The authors analyze the generated music from a musicological perspective and find that the model can preserve stylistic meaning and develop coherent phrase ideas. These findings suggest that the system can sustain musically sophisticated exchanges in the demonstrated setting. The contribution combines a responsive physical interface with an account of the musical continuity that makes alternating human and model contributions meaningful as a duet.
neurips-2025-the-ghost-in-the-keys-a-dis.tldr: Aria-Duet enables a pianist and generative model to exchange coherent musical phrases through a shared acoustic Disklavier piano.

paragraphs: This paper examines why some initialization strategies improve Low-Rank Adaptation, a parameter-efficient way to tune large models. Spectral initialization can improve learning but adds computational and storage costs. The authors argue that the magnitude of weight updates is the central mechanism behind these gains and use that explanation to design LoRAM.

Their analysis proves that low-rank structure intrinsically bounds update magnitudes. It connects learning rate, scaling, and initialization as different ways to regulate those magnitudes. The authors further attribute spectral initialization’s benefit to amplified updates, challenging the interpretation that its gains primarily come from knowledge encoded in spectral components.

LoRAM initializes the adaptation using deterministic orthogonal bases scaled according to pretrained weight magnitudes. This is intended to reproduce spectral methods’ gains without their added overhead. Across extensive experiments, the authors report matching or exceeding spectral initialization while retaining LoRA’s efficiency. The contribution combines an explanation of initialization behavior with a compact method that makes update magnitude an explicit design consideration.
neurips-2025-the-primacy-of-magnitude-in.tldr: LoRAM uses magnitude-scaled orthogonal initialization to match or outperform tested spectral LoRA methods while preserving efficiency.
